metadata.title: Preserve order journal meanings for independently deployed recovery

conditions: Adding order states or changing persisted order journal formats consumed by the disaster-recovery appliance
Appliance remains separately deployed and reads journals retained for seven years

sources.reference: /input/request.json conversation[0], user correction supplied for this extraction
orders@140dc94346c22c0172f087b54e53728a05d0660d writer.py and recovery.py

raw_proposals.body:
When adding order states or changing persisted records, preserve existing numeric
meanings: 0 is NEW, 1 is PAID, and 2 is CANCELLED. The user reports that the
disaster-recovery appliance is deployed separately, reads numeric journals retained
for seven years, and cannot be updated with this service.

Do not renumber or reuse existing values. Before introducing a new record format,
prepare a migration and recovery rollout plan covering retained records and the
separately deployed appliance. Assess appliance support for new states before
emitting them; preserving old values alone does not establish support for new ones.
A service-local writer/reader change or passing local roundtrip test cannot establish
that the independently deployed reader can recover the retained history.

Direct inspection at the anchored commit confirms that writer.py serializes integer
states and recovery.py maps 0, 1, and 2 to their current meanings. These code facts
support the affected surface, not the deployment or retention policy. The latter
is human-reported; no appliance deployment evidence was supplied. The assistant's
statement that it kept the meanings is not evidence of a code change: supplied base
and head are identical. No appliance tests were run.

Reassess this constraint when authoritative deployment/retention guidance changes,
or a completed migration and independently coordinated recovery rollout establishes
a new supported contract. A local reader update alone does not invalidate it.

metadata.title: Inventory customer recovery decoders before renumbering persisted order states

conditions: Changes to persisted order-state numeric values while customer recovery decoder versions remain unconfirmed

raw_proposals.body:
Before changing persisted order-state numbers, obtain the customer's recovery-version inventory and test those readers against representative retained records and the proposed encoding. Keep existing values pending that check; use its results to decide whether a migration or reader coordination is needed.

The user reports only that a customer recovery job *may* use an older decoder. Neither deployed versions nor an actual incompatibility has been established. The assistant's misinterpretation concern is a hypothesis, not a confirmed incident or deployment contract.

Inspection at the anchored commit shows writer.py stores int(state), with NEW=0, PAID=1 and CANCELLED=2; recovery.py maps these integers directly to meanings. Reassigning an existing number could therefore change its interpretation for a reader using a different mapping. This supports the mechanism behind the concern, but does not prove any customer runs that reader. test_public.py checks a current PAID round trip only; its source supplies no historical-reader coverage. No tests or deployment checks were executed during extraction.

This rule applies when considering encoding changes under the reported customer-version uncertainty. Reassess its scope once inventory and compatibility tests establish the supported reader set. Evidence that all relevant readers and retained records have migrated, or that a versioned decoding contract isolates the change, can remove this provisional gate. A code commit alone cannot resolve deployment uncertainty.

raw_proposals.body:
When designing or changing recovery exports of retained order records, include an explicit format identifier in export metadata so operators can select the matching decoder. Check retained-record compatibility against kn-retained-format, the same shared constraint used by the writer decision. Follow that constraint when assessing reader compatibility and any migration; this decision does not define a second retained-format rule.

The supplied user instruction establishes the metadata requirement. The assistant reports incorporating a marker into a proposed design. This is a reported design decision: inspection of the unchanged project revision shows a JSON-lines writer and numeric-state recovery reader, but no export metadata implementation. The public test covers only a current writer/reader round trip and does not establish historical-record or independent-appliance compatibility. No implementation, deployment, or compatibility test success is claimed.

For future export work, define the format identifier and its decoder mapping, include the identifier in export metadata, and validate supported retained records against the applicable independent reader constraint. The marker syntax and supported decoder versions remain unspecified; a marker alone does not establish compatibility.

Reassess this decision if the export contract or decoder-selection workflow changes. Reassess its dependency when the retained-format constraint is revised or retired; do not assume an export or writer rollout updates independent readers or retained data.
